title: Benefits of having a home gym: King in your own castle
summary: NH argues the main benefit of a home gym is total freedom: no rules against noise, deadlifting or intensity. He recounts being harassed out of his university gym for deadlifting and being told he was too intimidating, and claims commercial gyms' rules suppress the energy needed for gains. He warns against panic-buying equipment at inflated prices during the COVID gym closures.

claims.claim: Encouraging people to rush into building home gyms during the COVID closures is irresponsible; companies are exploiting the crisis and some prices have already doubled.
The best thing about a home gym is being able to train however you want: bang weights, scream, drop plates, be shirtless, blast music.
Modern commercial gyms have a laundry list of rules that turn them into kindergartens rather than places where you are left alone to train.
At his university gym a staff member decided he was not allowed to deadlift, followed him around and kicked him out whenever he started, which forced him to build his own gym.
He has been approached by gym staff and told he was too big and intimidating to other members.
Commercial gym environments are disconnected from what you need to make gains, which is fire and energy; they want quiet light curls and leg extensions.
He understands that grunting can be obnoxious, but some gyms will even ban you for the noise of racking an overhead press.
He has made far more progress since having his own gym; training as aggressively as you like unlocks something mentally that lets you push your limits.
In a commercial gym you may fail the last two reps of a set because you hold back from grunting so as not to scare people.
Gyms normalizing weak, wimpy behavior is destroying iron culture; if they destroy the churches, you must build your own temple.
Build a home gym deliberately once the crisis passes, rather than piling up equipment bought in a hurry.
